method_card.title: Identity and Self-Description
method_card.content:
This lesson covers how to introduce yourself and describe your identity in French — your nationality, the languages you speak, your values and what makes you who you are.

FrenchEnglish
je m'appellemy name is / I am called
j'ai [number] ansI am [number] years old
je suis [nationality]I am [nationality]
anglais(e)English
français(e)French
espagnol(e)Spanish
allemand(e)German
gallois(e)Welsh
écossais(e)Scottish
irlandais(e)Irish
je parle [language]I speak [language]
l'anglais / le français / l'espagnolEnglish / French / Spanish
mes valeursmy values
important(e) pour moiimportant to me

Nationality adjectives agree in gender and number with the person they describe. Masculine: anglais, français, espagnol, allemand, gallois, écossais, irlandais. Feminine: add -e (or change -ais → -aise, -ois → -oise): anglaise, française, espagnole, allemande, galloise, écossaise, irlandaise. Important: nationality adjectives are NOT capitalised in French (unlike in English).

être + adjective: Use être to describe identity and character: Je suis curieux et ouvert d'esprit. (I am curious and open-minded.) Adjectives must agree: masculine curieux, feminine curieuse.

Languages: Say je parle [language] or je parle couramment [language] (I speak [language] fluently). The language names are always lower case: l'anglais, le français, l'espagnol.

Model paragraph: Je m'appelle Sofia. J'ai seize ans et je suis anglaise. Je parle anglais et français. Pour moi, les valeurs les plus importantes sont l'honnêteté et la loyauté. Je suis curieuse et j'adore apprendre de nouvelles choses. (My name is Sofia. I am sixteen and I am English. I speak English and French. For me, the most important values are honesty and loyalty. I am curious and I love learning new things.)
steps: Learn nationality adjectives and remember they agree in gender — and are never capitalised
Practise introducing yourself using je m'appelle, j'ai [number] ans and je suis [nationality]
Describe the languages you speak using je parle + language noun
Write a full self-description combining nationality, languages and values

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — introductions and identity appear in every exam series

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Je suis anglais et je parle anglais et un peu de français.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break it down: Je suis anglais | et | je parle anglais | et un peu de français.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Je suis anglais = I am English. Notice anglais is lower case in French.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: je parle anglais = I speak English. un peu de = a little (of).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I am English and I speak English and a little French.

worked_examples.question: How do you make nationality adjectives agree in French?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Nationality adjectives agree with the person being described. Masculine form is the base: anglais, français, espagnol, gallois.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: To form the feminine, usually add -e. But watch patterns: -ais → -aise (anglais → anglaise), -ois → -oise (gallois → galloise), -ol → -ole (espagnol → espagnole).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Important: nationality adjectives in French are NOT capitalised. Write je suis anglais, not je suis Anglais.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Add -e (or follow the pattern) to form the feminine. Never capitalise nationality adjectives in French.

bronze.question: Match the French nationality adjectives to the English meaning
Match the French identity phrases to the English meaning

gaps.correct_explain: m'appelle is correct — je m'appelle = my name is / I am called.

wrong.appelle: appelle without the reflexive pronoun is incorrect. S'appeler is reflexive: je m'appelle.

gaps.rule: Verb avoir — j'ai (I have/I am for age)
gaps.correct_explain: ai is the je form of avoir. French uses avoir (to have) to express age: j'ai quinze ans = I am fifteen.

wrong.suis: suis is from être. For age in French, use avoir: j'ai quinze ans, not je suis quinze ans.

gaps.correct_explain: anglaise is the feminine form of anglais. Any feminine nationality is acceptable here.

wrong.anglais: anglais is masculine. The subject is je = Inès (feminine), so you need anglaise.

gaps.rule: Language noun — lower case, masculine article
gaps.correct_explain: anglais = English (language). Language names in French are lower case and use a definite article when needed.

bronze.question: What does 'Je suis galloise et je parle gallois et anglais' mean?
options: I am Welsh and I speak Welsh and English
I am Scottish and I speak Scottish and English
I am Irish and I speak Irish and English
I am Welsh and I speak French and English

model_answers: I am French and I live in Paris. I speak French and a little Spanish.
I am French and I live in Paris. I speak French and a little bit of Spanish.

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
silver.english: My name is Lucas. I am fifteen years old and I am Scottish.

gaps.correct_explain: ai is the je form of avoir. In French, use avoir to express age: j'ai quinze ans.

wrong.suis: suis is from être. For age, French uses avoir not être: j'ai quinze ans.

gaps.correct_explain: écossais is the masculine form (Lucas is male). Nationality adjectives are lower case in French.

wrong.Écossais: Nationality adjectives are lower case in French: écossais, not Écossais.
wrong.écossaise: écossaise is the feminine form. Lucas is male, so use écossais.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ma sœur est Irlandaise et elle parle irlandais et anglais.
silver.explanation: Nationality adjectives in French are never capitalised. Write irlandaise (lower case), not Irlandaise.
silver.translation: My sister is Irish and she speaks Irish and English.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: I speak French fluently and I am learning Spanish.

distractor_labels.le: l'espagnol uses the elided article l' before a vowel — not le. Use l'espagnol

silver.source_text: I am English and I live in Manchester. I speak English fluently but I am also learning French.
model_answers: Je suis anglais(e) et j'habite à Manchester. Je parle anglais couramment mais j'apprends aussi le français.
Je suis anglais et j'habite à Manchester. Je parle anglais couramment mais j'apprends aussi le français.

model_answers: Je m'appelle Amélie. J'ai quinze ans et je suis française. Je parle français et anglais couramment. Pour moi, les valeurs les plus importantes sont l'honnêteté et le respect.

gold.question: Build the sentence in French

distractor_labels.le: wrong gender — chose is feminine, so the superlative uses la plus, not le plus
distractor_labels.très: for superlatives use la plus + adjective, not très

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a leisure centre on a school exchange trip. The receptionist asks you about yourself.

bullets.prompt: Introduce yourself — say your name, age and nationality.
bullets.model_answer: Je m'appelle Jules. J'ai seize ans et je suis anglais.
bullets.note: je m'appelle; j'ai + age + ans; je suis + nationality adjective (lower case)

bullets.model_answer: Je parle anglais couramment et j'apprends le français depuis deux ans.
bullets.note: je parle + language; depuis + present tense for ongoing duration

bullets.prompt: Describe two values that are important to you.
bullets.model_answer: Pour moi, les valeurs les plus importantes sont l'honnêteté et la loyauté. Je trouve que la confiance est essentielle.
bullets.note: les valeurs les plus importantes; definite article with abstract nouns (l'honnêteté)

bullets.prompt: Ask the receptionist what activities are available at the leisure centre.
bullets.model_answer: Quelles activités sont disponibles ici, s'il vous plaît ?
bullets.note: question with quel/quelles + noun; formal register with s'il vous plaît

gold.correct_text: Je m'appelle Sofia. J'ai seize ans, je suis espagnole et je parle espagnol, anglais et un peu de français.

gold.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
gold.english: It is important that each person is respected for who they are.
sentence_parts: Il est important que chaque personne

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive — être after il est important que (Higher)
gaps.correct_explain: soit is the present subjunctive of être. After il est important que, French requires the subjunctive.

wrong.est: est is the indicative. After il est important que, you need the present subjunctive: soit.
wrong.sera: sera is the simple future. After que + subjunctive trigger, use soit.
